finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::iterate job mints an unscoped github app installation token and hands it to a bash-enabled agent running untrusted branch code

verdict.reasoning: The supplied agent-iterate-ci.yml "Generate GitHub App token" step (create-github-app-token@v1) passes only app-id and private-key — no `permission-*` inputs — so the minted token inherits the App installation's full permission set; it is then handed to actions/checkout (which persists it into .git/config by default, no `persist-credentials: false`) and to claude-code-action as `github_token`, in a job that runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on the branch and allows the Bash tool. The contrast the reviewer draws is accurate: the fix job in agent-review-panel.yml explicitly sets permission-contents/pull-requests/issues with the comment "this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code", and agent-implement.yml's branch-protection step notes the App needs Administration: read, so the installation is indeed broader than contents/PRs. Caveat: this token step is pre-existing code untouched by the diff under review (the diff only adds `allowed_bots` and the `fix` dependency in the stalled job), so it is a pre-existing hardening gap rather than a regression; the mitigating factors (fork rejection, base-repo agent/ branches only, AGENT_PIPELINE_ENABLED gate) limit but do not eliminate the exposure.
